title: Speed Limits & Stopping Distances
whatItIs: A speed limit is the absolute maximum, not a target. Drive so you can stop well within the distance you can see to be clear.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT exceed the limit. Roads with street lights: usually 30 mph (20 mph in Wales).
Cars MUST NOT exceed 60 mph on single carriageways, or 70 mph on dual carriageways and motorways.
Towing a caravan or trailer: MUST NOT exceed 50 mph single, 60 mph dual carriageway and motorway.

keyFacts: Gap: at least two seconds on high-speed roads; at least double it when wet, up to ten times on ice.

visual.caption: Typical stopping distances: a general guide (rule 126)

a.label: Thinking distance
points: Rises 3 m per 10 mph (6 m to 21 m)

b.label: Braking distance
points: 6 m at 20 mph, 75 m at 70 mph
Depends on road surface, weather, vehicle

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is driving at 60 mph. What is the typical overall stopping distance in the Highway Code?
onTheTest.why: Rule 126: 18 m thinking + 55 m braking = 73 m (240 feet).

onTheTest.question: Speed limit for a car towing a caravan on a motorway?
onTheTest.why: Rule 124 table: cars towing caravans or trailers, 50 mph on single carriageways, 60 mph on dual carriageways and motorways.

traps: Limits aren't targets: DT1 doesn't fault slowing for busy streets.
Holding up traffic is a fault too (DT1 Progress).
ABS should keep steering control, but don't assume it stops you in a shorter distance.

jurisdictionNotes.text: Roads with street lights: 20 mph in Wales (30 mph in England and Scotland), unless signs say otherwise.
